stages.title: Console Output
learningObjectives: Use console.log to output strings to standard output
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Console Output in JavaScript

In JavaScript (Node.js environment), outputting data to the terminal is done via `console.log()`.

```javascript
console.log("Hello, JavaScript!");
```
stages.problemStatementMd:

stages.lessonContentMd:
## Arithmetic Operators

JavaScript supports standard math operators:
- `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`
- `%` Modulo (remainder of division)

```javascript
console.log(10 % 3); // 1
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Modulo Shield

stages.lessonContentMd:
## Arrays in JavaScript

```javascript
const arr = [10, 20, 30];
console.log(arr.length); // 3
console.log(arr[0]);     // 10
console.log(arr[arr.length - 1]); // 30
```
stages.problemStatementMd:

stages.title: Array Method Filter
prerequisites: Mutate arrays using .push() and format output using .join(' ')
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Array Filter

`.filter()` creates a new array containing elements that pass a test callback:

```javascript
const nums = [1, 2, 3, 4];
const evens = nums.filter(x => x % 2 === 0);
console.log(evens.join(" ")); // "2 4"
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Signal Filter

Read space-separated integers. Use `.filter()` to extract numbers greater than `10`. Print them joined by spaces.

stages.title: Array Method Map
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Array Map

`.map()` creates a new array by applying a callback to each element:

```javascript
const nums = [1, 2, 3];
const doubled = nums.map(x => x * 2);
console.log(doubled.join(" ")); // "2 4 6"
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Signal Amplification

Read space-separated integers. Use `.map()` to square each number (`x * x`) and print them joined by spaces.
